how supported socialisation can help people with EMI to ‘be social’.
the role of social capital and social integration in the lives of service users with enduring mental illness.
how socialisation can be a catalyst for positive social change.

supported socialisation can be an important intervention in addressing the social exclusion of people with enduring psychiatric illness.
supported socialisation is a potentially valuable intervention for people with enduring mental illnesses.

supported socialisation can help people with EMI to develop social skills and confidence, and to overcome the social isolation and stigma that often accompany mental illness, thus enhancing their quality of life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supported socialisation can be a powerful tool in facilitating social integration for people with EML.
supported socialisation has a positive impact on the lives of people experiencing mental illness and can be an important part of a recovery-oriented service provision.
the programme is an important intervention for people with EME and that the socialising experience is a positive one for most people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supported socialisation is an important and under-utilised resource in the lives of those with EMI.
supported socialisation programmes can be a powerful intervention in the lives of service users with mental illness.
socialisation can be a powerful tool in the recovery of people with EMI, and should be prioritised in the recovery journey.
